text: In supervised learning, a model learns from labelled examples. Each training example contains input features and a target label. The model predicts labels from input features. A loss function measures the difference between predicted labels and target labels. Gradient descent updates model parameters to reduce the loss. Training minimises loss over many labelled examples. We now turn to evaluation on unseen data. We split our data into training, validation, and test sets. The test set must remain separate from model training. A validation set helps us select model hyperparameters. Repeatedly selecting models using test scores leaks information. Test performance should estimate generalisation to unseen examples. Finally, consider the ethical impact of data collection. Consent and privacy matter when collecting personal information. Data subjects should understand the purpose of collection. A dataset can reproduce historical discrimination. We should examine performance across demographic groups. Protecting privacy and auditing fairness are responsibilities throughout deployment.
